How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02723 (fare breakdown EV-FARE-02723, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded in full. The ground is limb (d) of POL-NS-01. That limb requires the trip to have been ended by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02723) shows it was ended by the driver at 12:06:23 under DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which the clause states in terms is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and does not satisfy limb (d). The driver's chat message of 12:00:29 ('cannot find you, where are you') and his statement 'Could not locate the rider so I cancelled' say the same thing. The driver does not ask the Judge to read that code as one of the three, and the failure is dispositive: the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause (Rider claim 1 accepted; Driver claim 7 accepted only as a labelling error, whose consequence POL-NS-01 fixes as below). The driver did reach the pickup and did wait. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02723, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) places him 0 m from the pin and stationary at the 11:59:59 'I'm Here' tap, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and the arrival marker is not false (Driver claim 3 accepted). He then held position inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a single continuous run of 380 seconds, 11:59:59 to 12:06:19, against the 180-second free waiting period in force on this record (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies). There is therefore no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06 (Driver claim 4 accepted) and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied (Driver claim 2 accepted). Limb (c) alone does not make the fee chargeable, because limb (d) breaks. Because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, POL-NS-01 states the consequence itself: the fee is not chargeable, the ruling is a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and the mis-selected reason code is recorded in the referrals as a driver-education item. That is this ruling (Rider claim 2 accepted). The rider's own conduct does not alter it: POL-NS-04 independently exonerates the rider — she sent a locating message ('at the lift lobby') at 12:00:59; the driver neither replied within 120 seconds of it nor placed an in-app call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty); and her device recorded 67 qualifying fixes, all within about 15.5 m of the pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius (Rider claim 3 accepted). Both routes agree. Driver compensation: none. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (d) is not, so the condition precedent fails and the payout is never reached (Rider claim 4 accepted).
